intended_object: The inner wall (the "D-wall") of the unit-width hallway rotated by angle t and translated to support the cap K. It is the line {p : ⟨p, n(t+π/2)⟩ = h_K(t+π/2) − 1}, where n(θ) = (cos θ, sin θ) and h_K is the support function of K. The definition gives this line as the graph y = m·x + b, recorded as the pair (m, b). This reading comes from the docstring and from how `innerQuadrant` and `capBoundaryHeight` use it.
explanation:
The library defines `supportValue s θ` as sup ⟨p, (cos θ, sin θ)⟩ over p ∈ s. The second half-plane in `innerQuadrant` has boundary ⟨p, n(t+π/2)⟩ = h_K(t+π/2) − 1. Since n(t+π/2) = (−sin t, cos t), that boundary is −sin t·x + cos t·y = h − 1. When cos t ≠ 0 this gives y = (sin t/cos t)·x + (h − 1)/cos t, which is exactly the pair (sin t / cos t, (h − 1)/cos t) the definition returns.

The definition is only used for t in Θ.directions ⊂ (0, π/2), where cos t > 0. The lemma `mem_innerQuadrant_iff_lt_min_affine` confirms that the open half-plane is exactly the region below this line. The companion `capBAffine` describes the other wall in the same way.

This is a specific line from the moving sofa construction. Writing it in slope-intercept form over ℝ² is what the construction needs, so it is not too narrow, and Mathlib has no counterpart for it. A value at cos t = 0 would be a junk value, but it never arises in use.
